Until others start using drones on us. Whether by building their own, or hacking ours.

Ah yes. We're always on the bleeding-edge of warfare. Our tech is too fragile, good for fighting undeveloped countries, but the other major world powers have been building weapons specifically to counter us.

Not just major world powers. Drones are going to level the playing field in favour of groups like ISIS and Al-Qaeda. We'd never have to worry about them getting F-18s or similar because fighter jets are extremely expensive and require a very skilled pilot. Drones don't have either of these limitations, so they make it possible for even small, fractured terrorist groups to launch attacks from the sky.

Not that I'm saying this could have been avoided if the US military wasn't developing the technology so much. Drones would have happened eventually since they have great peaceful applications as well. But long-term, I think drones will cause more problems than they solve for the US and allies. It takes away one big advantage we've always held.

The quote is quite relevant to drones, but it might not seem so right now.

Those anti-drone measures are interesting. I wasn't necessarily thinking of ISIS having a Predator-style drone. The missiles alone would probably be out of their price range. But they could certainly use a smaller and cheaper drone as a delivery system for an explosive, chemical, biological, or radioactive payload in a way never before possible. At the very least, the technology provides them with new opportunities.

One way to tie this to the quote would be to say: "Every successful attempt to make war easier and safer will also make it easier and safer for the enemy, which in turn may result in humiliation and disaster.".
